title: Count Square Submatrices with All Ones
spaceBreakdown:
- int ans, m, n, i, j: O(1)
- matrix modified in place: not counted (input)
approach: Use DP where dp[i][j] = side length of the largest all-ones square with bottom-right corner at (i,j). If matrix[i][j]=0, dp[i][j]=0; otherwise dp[i][j] = 1 + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1], dp[i-1][j-1]). The key insight: dp[i][j]=k means exactly k all-ones squares end at (i,j) (sides 1 through k), so the answer is the sum of all dp values. We modify the matrix in place for O(1) extra space.
hints: For each cell containing a 1, how many all-ones squares have that cell as their bottom-right corner, and what determines that count?

Dynamic programming: let dp[i][j] be the side length of the largest all-ones square with bottom-right corner at (i,j). In Example 1, cell (2,3) has dp[1][3]=2, dp[2][2]=2, dp[1][2]=2, so dp[2][3] = 1 + min(2,2,2) = 3.

**Single cell** - only one element, no neighbors to reference
`Input: [[1]]` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: accessing matrix[i-1][j-1] without checking i>0 and j>0 → out of bounds access

**All zeros** - no squares possible
`Input: [[0,0],[0,0]]` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: computing 1 + min(neighbors) before checking matrix[i][j]==0 → returns 1

**Single column** - no left neighbor exists
`Input: [[1],[1],[1]]` → `Expected: 3`
⚠️ Bug: accessing matrix[i][j-1] without checking j>0 → out of bounds access

**Two neighbors instead of three** - diagonal neighbor omitted
`Input: [[1,1,1],[1,0,1],[1,1,1]]` → `Expected: 8`
⚠️ Bug: using min of only matrix[i-1][j] and matrix[i][j-1] (omitting matrix[i-1][j-1]) → dp[2][2] becomes 2 instead of 1, returns 9

followUps.q: Count all axis-aligned rectangles (not just squares) with all ones.
followUps.a: Use a histogram-based approach: for each row, maintain column heights of consecutive ones, then use a monotonic stack to count rectangles ending at each row. TC: O(m*n), SC: O(n).

followUps.q: What if you cannot modify the input matrix?
followUps.a: Use two 1D arrays - dp[j] for the current row and prev[j] for the previous row. When matrix[i][j]=1, dp[j] = 1 + min(prev[j], dp[j-1], prev[j-1]); otherwise dp[j]=0. Swap after each row. TC: O(m*n), SC: O(n).

followUps.q: Count only squares with exactly side length k.
followUps.a: After computing dp[i][j] in place, count cells where dp[i][j] >= k. Each such cell is the bottom-right corner of at least one square of side k. TC: O(m*n), SC: O(1).
